cars.name: BMW X5 Le Mans
search: BMW X5 V12 Le Mans prototype
cars.notes: One-off X5 with the 6.1 L V12 from the Le Mans-winning V12 LMR, about 700 hp. Lapped the Nürburgring Nordschleife in under 8 minutes with Hans-Joachim Stuck.

cars.name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR
cars.location: Mostly Mercedes-Benz, Stuttgart; one at the Cité de l'Automobile, Mulhouse
cars.notes:
W196S sports-racing car that won the 1955 World Sportscar Championship. Wikipedia: 9 chassis built, 7 open race cars and 2 coupés; one (0006/55) destroyed at Le Mans, so 8 survive. Sources disagree: Supercar Nostalgia says eight in some places and nine in others; Ultimatecarpage lists 0009/55 as never completed and 0010/55 as a test car.

Chassis 0007/55 and 0008/55 became the Uhlenhaut Coupés, tracked as their own entry (Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé).

cars.name: 300 SLR 0001/54
cars.notes: The first 300 SLR. Moss 2nd at the 1955 Eifelrennen (#3), its only race. Shown for years at the Henry Ford Museum, Dearborn, then returned to Stuttgart.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0002/55
cars.notes: Development car and team spare (T-car at the Tourist Trophy and Targa Florio). Never raced. Registered AW 84 7984.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0003/55 "Fangio"
cars.notes: Fangio's car: 2nd in the Mille Miglia (#658, solo), won the Eifelrennen and the Swedish GP, 3rd at the Tourist Trophy, 2nd at the Targa Florio (Fangio/Kling), which clinched the 1955 title.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0004/55 "722"
cars.notes: Moss and Jenkinson won the 1955 Mille Miglia as #722, a record that still stands. Also won the Tourist Trophy (Moss/Fitch) and the Targa Florio (Moss/Collins). Raced in all six 1955 events and won three. Often called the most valuable car in the world.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0005/55 "Schlumpf"
cars.location: Cité de l'Automobile, Mulhouse, France (Schlumpf Collection)
cars.notes: Kling crashed out of the Mille Miglia (#701), 2nd at the Tourist Trophy (Fangio/Kling), 4th at the Targa Florio. Lent to the Schlumpf brothers in 1966; stayed after the French state bought the collection in 1981.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0006/55 "Le Mans #20"
cars.notes: Pierre Levegh / John Fitch, #20. Destroyed in the 1955 Le Mans disaster, which killed Levegh and 83 spectators. Earlier crashed by Herrmann in the Mille Miglia (#704). The sources don't say what became of the wreckage.

cars.name: 300 SLR 0010/55 "test car"
cars.notes: Listed only by Ultimatecarpage: the last 300 SLR built in 1955, used to test new parts, never raced. Supercar Nostalgia doesn't list it.

cars.name: Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé
cars.location: One at the Mercedes-Benz Museum, Stuttgart. The other sold in 2022 for €135M to a private collector.
cars.notes: Only two prototypes were ever made—one nicknamed "Red" (chassis 8) and the other "Blue" (chassis 7), differentiated by their interior upholstery colors.  In May 2022, Mercedes-Benz sold the red Uhlenhaut Coupé at a private RM Sotheby's auction for €135 million (roughly $142–143 million), making it the most expensive car ever sold in history. The proceeds went toward the global Mercedes-Benz Fund for environmental and decarbonization scholarships. The second car ("Blue") remains in the collection of the Mercedes-Benz Museum in Stuttgart

cars.name: Uhlenhaut Coupé "Red"
cars.location: Private collector (sold May 2022, RM Sotheby's private auction, €135M)
